title: UiKit dom_button element
description: What a kit component forwards to the <button> element it renders: React's own DOM attributes for that element, declared once here by hand rather than re-derived per component. Hand-written on purpose - React's button attributes are the same surface for every component that renders a button, and the roughly 285 individually-named attributes and event handlers React's own types declare for a button carry no kit-specific fact, so listing them per component produced a file no reader ever opened. A prop the primitive library declares for its own part is NOT here: that is the component's own API and lives in its contract's `properties` (see extract.ts's declaration-site classification). Completeness is deliberately unverified: nothing compares this file against what a component actually forwards, so an attribute it does not name is classified as unknown rather than rejected, and the enrollment report prints the ones no surface declares.

children.description: TS: ReactNode. Not expressible in JSON Schema, checked by tsc.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties. Not expressible in JSON Schema, checked by tsc. A component wrapping a primitive part widens this to accept a function of the part's state, which is why nothing is asserted here.

value.description: TS: string | number | readonly string[]. Not expressible in JSON Schema, checked by tsc.

^aria-.description: Any ARIA attribute passes. Enumerating the WAI-ARIA set here would go stale against the spec and buy nothing: a contract's job is to stop typos in KIT props, and the a11y rules that actually matter (icon-only needs aria-label) are invariants, not a property list.

^data-.description: Any data attribute passes: they are open by construction, and consumers add their own (data-testid being the common one).

^on[A-Z].description: Any React event handler passes. React declares roughly 150 of them by literal name per element; a contract that named each one would restate React's own type definitions and go stale against them, and no kit fact lives in any single entry.

$comment: Intentionally NOT closed (no unevaluatedProperties/additionalProperties): a component's contract does not derive from this type, it HOLDS its id (x-gts-traits.host_element), and whoever needs the surface applies it beside the contract - so this schema cannot know what else applies to the same props object. A component's own derived type is what classifies a prop nothing here or there evaluates.
